name: Light Moss Green
lede: Light Moss Green pales [[moss-green]] toward yellow, filed by the ISCC-NBS in 1955 and rarely found in our painting archive before the 1860s.

sections.title: A paled moss
sections.body: The name is the modifier *light* set against the base color [[moss-green]] [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 Circular 553 files the matching range as block 106, "light olive," a Delta-E of 7.8 from this hex; the xkcd 2010 crowd survey records the same compound independently [1]. Nearest on file are [[pale-olive-green]] at 2.6 units and [[pistachio]] at 3.4, both close enough to read as the same family at a glance [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this shade, as photographed, in 9 of 23,781 paintings, 0.04 percent; within a single canvas it is a distinct area in 6 of them, rarer than 73 percent of our named colors [2]. The earliest dated match is an 1861 painting, 94 years before the name's 1955 record; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first, and a hue match in an aged photograph is not proof of a dye or pigment [2].

origin.named_after: the modifier light applied to the base color moss-green
origin.first_recorded: 1955 (ISCC-NBS, National Bureau of Standards Circular 553, block 106)
